projects.title: Using a Neural Network to Identify Respiratory Crackles in Wireless Stethoscope Data
projects.description: This project won an Honorable Mention at the Synopsys Championship. My research involved creating a CNN-BLSTM model for detecting respiratory crackles. I optimized this model to have a precision of 90+% when detecting crackles.

My Software Engineering internship at Shopify has come to an end. I’m so grateful for the past 4 months, working alongside some of the most talented, supportive, and innovative people I’ve ever met. During my time here, I had the opportunity to work on the bleeding edge of AI tech, helping build a chatbot and contributing to several other exciting projects. A huge thank you to my incredible mentor Emmanuel Kaunitz for his guidance and support, my manager Curtis Traverse , my amazing team, and the early talent team who made this whole experience possible. I learned so much—not just about tech, but also about collaboration, creativity, and the value of constantly iterating and improving. Excited to take everything I’ve learned into the next chapter! 🚀

Yesterday we had the incredible opportunity to finally present our PLAN211 project of a 100-year Laurel Greenway Vision to an amazing group of panelists. I am so beyond proud to have been able to work with Mya Mistry , Matthew Hwang , Isaac Nathaniel Leung , and Haris Wilkinson over our 4 month long term. I couldn’t have asked for a better team! Through many days and late nights spent in the Planning Studio, brainstorming ideas and more ideas, we were able to come up “Grey to Green” driven by the idea of creating a pedestrian oriented urban-ecological corridor where users are able to experience nature within the urban heart of Waterloo, as well as facilitate a safe, green way to cross the city. This process has been hard and long but truly so rewarding and I am so so grateful for everything I have learned and the memories I’ve been able to make. I would like to extend a huge thank you to our instructor Hadi El-shayeb for always pushing us past our comfort zone and our TAs, Myah Sachedina , Maya Van de Mosselaer and Michael Barone for their continous support throughout the term. It is hard to believe this term is over but I am so excited for the rest of my journey in urban design!

🔵 A few weeks ago, my buddies and I had the opportunity to participate in MakeUofT. Where we built a real-time hand-tracking glove with haptic feedback for VR – an ambitious and inspiring challenge to complete in a matter of 2 days. 🚀 🔹 In simple terms, our idea was to produce a glove which would replace VR controllers. Actions like grabbing, throwing, carrying and manipulating objects within a game are essential for creating an immersive and interactive experience, allowing players to engage with the virtual environment in a more natural and intuitive way. By accurately tracking hand movements and providing real-time feedback, these interactions enhance gameplay realism and player engagement. 🦾 🎮 🔹 𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐝𝐢𝐝 𝐈 𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐫𝐢𝐛𝐮𝐭𝐞? - Established Bluetooth serial communication between Windows and an Arduino via the HC-05 module. ✅ - Debugged and fine-tuned firmware including solving baud rate mismatches to ensure the reliable data transmission. ✅ - Burned and configured the Arduino bootloader to ensure proper setup.✅ - Designing and implementing the control system, enabling Bluetooth communication between Arduino to adjust servo motor power, which in turn generated haptic feedback in the glove. ✅ 🔹 This isn’t the end though. Our goal is to ensure consistent Bluetooth communication, enhance the haptic response—ideally replacing the current model with a more effective tension mechanism—and develop a more streamlined setup for mounting all the project’s components on the arm. I'd like to thank my teammates Dhruva Shekdar Syed Hashmi and Connor Sequeira for making this an exceptional experience, and thanks to MakeUofT for the opportunity!

I’m excited to reveal what we’ve been working on for the last 9 months at DocuBridge —the AI Excel add-in for finance! Anyone in finance knows how long it takes to build financial models. Wrangling data from multiple sources, reformatting it into a specific format, and mapping data and formulas is always a pain to deal with. DocuBridge is the first AI-based Excel plugin designed to make the financial modeling process 100x easier. It’s simple - you just save one of your old models as a template, select your data source(s), and DocuBridge creates models in your format, within seconds. Our vision is to build the first end-to-end finance copilot to save people in finance hundreds of hours, with our AI tools built directly into Excel. I’m lucky to build this with my cofounder Dhruv Kulkarni and the rest of the team. Thank you to everyone who has supported us on this journey so far. If this looks like it might save you some time, drop a comment or reach out—we’d love to hear from you!
